body:
Every model argument in the package is a **character string** that gets parsed with `as.formula()`:

```r
ec_ipw(ps_formula = "S ~ x1 + x2")                    # string
did_ec_ipw(trt_formula = "A ~ x1 + x2")               # string
ec_aipw(outcome_formula = c("y1 ~ x1", "y2 ~ x1"))    # vector of strings
```

R users expect `S ~ x1 + x2`. Strings cost tab completion, syntax highlighting, and any editor help; a typo in the model becomes a runtime `as.formula()` failure rather than a parse error at the call site. Formulas also carry their environment, which strings discard.

Affected slots, all currently `"character"`:

| Constructor | Arguments |
|---|---|
| `ec_ipw()` | `ps_formula` |
| `ec_aipw()` | `ps_formula`, `outcome_formula` |
| `did_ec_ipw()` | `ps_formula`, `trt_formula` |
| `did_ec_aipw()` | `ps_formula`, `trt_formula`, `outcome_formula` |
| `did_ec_or()` | `outcome_formula_ext`, `outcome_formula_rct_ctrl`, `outcome_formula_rct_trt` |

## The complication

The strings are not passed through untouched. `estimate()` rewrites the left-hand side so the formula matches the column names given to `setup_analysis_*()`:

```r
ps_formula <- sub("^[^~]*~", paste0(trial_status, " ~"), method@ps_formula)
```

Six call sites do this (`R/ec_ipw.R:128`, `R/ec_aipw.R:135`, `R/did_ec_ipw.R:85,88`, `R/did_ec_aipw.R:98,101`). So whatever you write on the left of `~` is discarded — `ec_ipw(ps_formula = "anything ~ x1 + x2")` works identically to `"S ~ x1 + x2"`, which is itself worth surfacing.

That is regex on a string. The formula equivalent is cleaner, not harder:

```r
reformulate(attr(terms(f), "term.labels"), response = trial_status)
```

## Suggested approach

1. Widen the slots to a `formulaOrCharacter` class union and accept both.
2. Normalize once at construction with `stats::as.formula()`, so the internals only ever see formulas.
3. Replace the six `sub()` calls with `reformulate()`.
4. Deprecate strings with a `lifecycle` warning; keep them working for several releases. There are 96 named `ps_formula =` call sites in this repo alone, plus whatever users have written against CRAN.
5. Update vignettes, tests and examples.

Accepting both indefinitely is also defensible — the cost is one `as.formula()` call and a slightly wider `@param`.

## Related

Interacts with #63. Once `ps_fit` exists, `ps_formula` is one of several ways to specify the propensity model, and making it a real formula sharpens the distinction: a formula means the package fits and owns the model, a function or fitted object means the user supplies weights. Worth doing after #63 lands so the two changes do not collide in the same files.

Also worth deciding alongside: `ec_ipw()` and `ec_aipw()` have no `trt_formula` at all, unlike the DID pair, so they cannot express stratified randomization. Same estimator family, different capability.
title: Accept real formulas, not formula strings
